papers.authors: Lu S, Girard N, Yang JC, Shepherd FA, Dong X, Arulananda S, Metro G, Hayashi H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical Oncology, Shanghai Chest Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, School of Medicine, Shanghai.
papers.results: 主要终点PFS（盲法独立中心评估）：疾病进展或死亡HR 0.55（95%CI 0.42–0.72），P<0.001；OS：死亡HR 0.68（95%CI 0.50–0.91），P=0.01（最终分析）；12个月PFS率36% vs 10%，12个月OS率70% vs 53%；治疗期间最常见不良事件为外周水肿（49%）、贫血（26%）、腹泻（26%）；≥3级不良事件64% vs 63%
papers.authors_conclusion: 在奥希替尼治疗期间进展、伴MET过表达或MET扩增或两者兼有的EGFR突变局部晚期或转移性NSCLC患者中，奥希替尼-赛沃替尼较铂类-培美曲塞显著延长无进展生存和总生存（由阿斯利康资助；SAFFRON，NCT05261399）

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Savolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy. METHODS: In this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety. RESULTS: Of the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; P<0.001), as well as significantly longer overall survival (hazard ratio for death, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.91; P = 0.01; final analysis). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of 12-month progression-free survival was 36% in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and 10% in the platinum-pemetrexed group, and the estimate of 12-month overall survival was 70% and 53%, respectively. The most frequently reported adverse events that occurred during treatment in the osimertinib-savolitinib group were peripheral edema (in 49% of the patients), anemia (in 26%), and diarrhea (in 26%). Grade 3 or higher adverse events during treatment were reported in 64% of the patients in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and in 63% of those in the platinum-pemetrexed group. CONCLUSIONS: Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: MET amplification accounts for up to 30% of acquired resistance to EGFR-TKI, especially following third-generation EGFR-TKI treatment, yet precision-targeted therapeutic options remain limited. Early-phase studies demonstrated promising antitumor activity with the MET-TKI dalmelitinib combined with the third-generation EGFR-TKI aumolertinib. This phase 3 trial compared dalmelitinib-aumolertinib with platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated, MET-amplified advanced NSCLC after EGFR-TKIs progression. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This randomized, open-label, phase 3 trial (NCT06110663) enrolled patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutated, MET-amplified NSCLC after EGFR-TKI progression. MET amplification was defined by fluorescence in situ hybridization as a mean MET copy number ≥5 or MET/CEP7 ratio ≥2. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to dalmelitinib-aumolertinib or platinum-based chemotherapy groups. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review per RECIST 1.1. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, objective response rate (ORR), duration of response (DoR), and safety. RESULTS: A total of 314 enrolled patients were assigned to dalmelitinib-aumolertinib (n=156) or platinum-based chemotherapy (n=158). Median follow-up was 11.2 months at the data cutoff date (December 10, 2025). Median PFS was 6.2 months with dalmelitinib-aumolertinib and 4.4 months with chemotherapy (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.45 to 0.81; P <0.001). Corresponding ORRs were 59.6% and 38.6%, and median DoRs were 9.7 months and 4.4 months, respectively. Overall survival data were immature. Grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 50.0% and 51.0% of patients, respectively. Toxicity profiles differed, with more hepatic laboratory abnormalities with dalmelitinib-aumolertinib and more hematologic toxicities with chemotherapy. CONCLUSION: The dalmelitinib-aumolertinib combination significantly improved PFS versus chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile in advanced EGFR-mutated, MET-amplified NSCLC after progression on EGFR-TKI. These findings support dual EGFR/ MET inhibition as a new treatment option in this biomarker selected population.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer have poor outcomes, with a median overall survival of approximately 12 to 13 months. Tarlatamab (a bispecific T-cell engager targeting delta-like ligand 3 [DLL3] and CD3) was previously shown to improve survival as second-line therapy. Whether adding tarlatamab to durvalumab (an anti-programmed death ligand 1 agent) after initial chemoimmunotherapy could significantly improve survival in the context of maintenance therapy after first remission has been unclear. METHODS: In this phase 3, international, open-label, randomized trial, we compared tarlatamab-durvalumab with durvalumab as first-line maintenance therapy in patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer without progression after initial chemoimmunotherapy. Overall survival and progression-free survival were assessed from randomization at the start of maintenance therapy as the primary and key secondary end points, respectively. Results of the prespecified interim analysis (data-cutoff date, July 7, 2026) are reported here. RESULTS: A total of 563 patients were randomly assigned to receive tarlatamab-durvalumab (282 patients) or durvalumab (281 patients). At a median follow-up of 15.9 months in the tarlatamab-durvalumab group and 16.1 months in the durvalumab group, the estimated median overall survival was 21.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 20.8 to could not be estimated) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 12.7 months (95% CI, 11.2 to 14.8) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for death, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32 to 0.54; P<0.001). The median progression-free survival was 7.4 months (95% CI, 5.6 to 9.1) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 1.9 months (95% CI, 1.9 to 2.0) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.28 to 0.42; P<0.001). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 46.8% of the patients who received tarlatamab-durvalumab and in 40.6% of those who received durvalumab alone. Cytokine release syndrome, mainly of grade 1 or 2, was seen in nearly half the patients receiving tarlatamab-durvalumab. CONCLUSIONS: Tarlatamab-durvalumab maintenance therapy resulted in significantly longer overall survival and progression-free survival than durvalumab alone among patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. (Funded by Amgen and AstraZeneca; DeLLphi-305 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06211036.).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal. METHODS: In this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis. RESULTS: A total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; P<0.001). An objective response occurred in 50.2% and 47.3% of the patients, respectively, and the median duration of response was 13.6 months and 6.8 months. Overall survival data were immature; the hazard ratio for death was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.38 to 0.88). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher that occurred after the start of treatment were reported in 47.6% of the patients assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab and in 60.6% of those assigned to receive chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Stomatitis was common with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab, but the events were predominantly grade 1 or 2. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. (Funded by Sichuan Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical; OptiTROP-Lung06 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06711900.).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pembrolizumab, alone or combined with platinum-based chemotherapy, is a standard first-line treatment for patients with metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable oncogenic alterations and with high programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression. We conducted a head-to-head comparison of these two treatment strategies. METHODS: In this multicenter, phase III trial (PERSEE, NCT04547504), adult patients with treatment-naïve stage IV or unresectable stage III NSCLC not amenable to definitive radiotherapy and PD-L1 expression ≥50% were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive pembrolizumab (200 mg every 3 weeks, for up to 35 cycles) or pembrolizumab in combination with four cycles of induction chemotherapy, stratified according to the presence of brain metastases and histologic subtype. Patients with non-squamous histology received cisplatin or carboplatin (AUC 5) plus pemetrexed, followed by pembrolizumab-pemetrexed maintenance; patients with squamous histology received carboplatin (AUC 6) plus paclitaxel, followed by pembrolizumab maintenance. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), assessed by blinded central review according to RECIST v1.1. Key secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), objective response rate, duration of response, and safety. RESULTS: A total of 321 patients underwent randomization, with 160 assigned to pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy and 161 to pembrolizumab monotherapy. At a median follow-up of 38.7 months, median PFS was significantly longer with combination therapy than with monotherapy (16.1 months [95% CI, 11.0-34.1] vs. 6.9 months [95% CI, 5.5-9.3]; hazard ratio (HR), 0.56; 95% CI, 0.43-0.74; P<0.001). Median OS was 50.2 months versus 29.9 months, respectively (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.56-1.05). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 54% and 19% of patients, respectively; grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events occurred in 13% of patients in each group. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with treatment-naïve advanced NSCLC and high PD-L1 expression, the addition of platinum-based chemotherapy to pembrolizumab significantly prolonged PFS compared with pembrolizumab monotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Divarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib. METHODS: In this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival, confirmed overall response, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, and safety. RESULTS: A total of 338 patients received divarasib (167 patients) or control treatment (171 patients; 156 received sotorasib and 15 received adagrasib). The median follow-up was 14.3 months. The median progression-free survival was 9.8 months with divarasib and 5.7 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.44 to 0.76; P<0.001). The median overall survival was 17.7 months with divarasib and 12.0 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for death, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.78; P<0.001). Of the 328 patients who could be evaluated for response, a confirmed response occurred in 58.4% in the divarasib group and in 32.3% in the control group. The median duration of response was 11.9 months with divarasib and 6.9 months with control treatment. Fewer grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were noted with divarasib (24.6%) than with control treatment (34.5%). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC, divarasib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than control treatment. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is highly lethal owing to its early and aggressive metastasis, yet the underlying multi-layer molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood, limiting therapeutic advances. METHODS: We performed integrative multi-omics profiling (including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and lactylome) on 99 matched primary tumor, metastatic lymph nodes, and normal esophagus tissue samples from 36 patients with metastatic ESCC. Molecular changes and cross-omics interactions associated with the metastatic cascades were characterized. Key findings were validated by immunohistochemistry and survival analysis in an independent cohort of 116 ESCC patients. Further functional and mechanistic studies were conducted using in vitro and a tail-vein experimental lung metastasis model. RESULTS: Our analysis revealed pronounced disturbance in immune-related pathways closely associated with metastatic progression and poor prognosis. Intercellular adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM1) was identified as a critical factor of ESCC invasion and metastasis. Additionally, lysine-lactylated proteins were predominantly involved in cytoskeleton, focal adhesion and glycolysis pathways during ESCC metastasis. Integrative analysis revealed that the lactylome interacts with the genome and transcriptome through both cis- and trans-regulatory mechanisms, primarily in immune and metabolic pathways. Notably, lactylation of phosphoglycerate mutase 1 (PGAM1) at residue K251 enhances its interaction with actin gamma 1 and promotes metastatic phenotypes. ICAM1 and PGAM1 K251 lactylation represent two independent metastasis-associated mechanisms identified from the same multi-omics dataset. CONCLUSIONS: This integrative multi-omics characterization provides a comprehensive resource for metastatic ESCC research and identifies K251-lactylated PGAM1 as a candidate prognostic biomarker and mechanistic lead warranting further preclinical validation.

papers.abstract_en: Advanced thymic carcinoma is a rare, aggressive malignancy with limited treatment options after chemotherapy failure. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (AL3810-202) aimed to evaluate lucitanib, a novel, orally potent tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR1‒3, FGFR1‒3, and PDGFRα/β in patients with advanced thymic carcinoma progressing after chemotherapy. Sixty-eight patients were randomized (2:1) to receive 10 mg lucitanib daily (n = 46) or placebo (n = 22). Although this study did not meet its primary endpoint of independent review committee (IRC)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS) (median 5.8 vs. 3.7 months; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.60; p = 0.1050), the prespecified log-rank test may have underestimated the treatment effect due to an observed non-proportional hazards pattern. Subsequent restricted mean survival time analysis demonstrated a statistically significant PFS benefit (p < 0.05), which was further supported by significantly prolonged investigator-assessed PFS (6.6 vs. 1.9 months; HR: 0.53; p = 0.0306). The most common grade 3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were hypertension (50%), proteinuria (15.2%), and thrombocytopenia (8.7%), with no grade 4/5 events. Considering the totality of the evidence and an acceptable safety profile, lucitanib may confer a meaningful clinical benefit for patients with advanced thymic carcinoma, warranting further investigation.

papers.abstract_en: Purpose ENTRÉE Lung (NCT03739710) was a global, open-label, platform study investigating novel immunotherapy combinations in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) following progression on anti-PD-(L)1 and platinum-based treatment. We report findings with dostarlimab (anti-PD-1) plus belrestotug (anti-TIGIT) with or without nelistotug (anti-CD96). Patients and Methods The study included safety cohorts with dose escalation and expansion: Arm 4 safety cohort (Arm4-safety), dostarlimab 500 mg plus belrestotug 200-1000 mg (initial dose level: 400 mg); Arm5-safety, dostarlimab 500 mg plus belrestotug 400 mg and nelistotug 210-1400 mg (initial dose level: 700 mg); study treatments were administered intravenously every 3 weeks. A randomized cohort was added to Arm 5 (Arm5-randomized), assigning patients to nelistotug 210 or 1400 mg in the triplet combination. Primary endpoints were safety and tolerability. Results Sixty-two patients were enrolled (n=24 Arm4-safety; n=17 Arm5-safety; n=21 Arm5-randomized [n=11, 200 mg; n=10, 1400 mg]). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 4 (17%), 1 (6%) and 3 (14%) patients in Arm4-safety, Arm5-safety and Arm5-randomized, respectively. There were few treatment discontinuations due to adverse events. Most patients exhibited progressive disease as best response. There was one partial response (Arm5-randomized, 210 mg); stable disease ≥12 weeks was experienced by 4 (17%), 5 (29%) and 2 (10%) patients in Arm4-safety, Arm5-safety and Arm5-randomized, respectively. Conclusions Dostarlimab plus belrestotug, with or without nelistotug, was well tolerated but demonstrated no clinically meaningful activity in previously treated advanced NSCLC. Further research is required to identify patients who may benefit from other immunotherapy combinations.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Anastomotic leakage after oesophagectomy is common, and associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence angiography has emerged as a promising intraoperative adjunct for perfusion assessment at the anastomotic site. This study aims to assess the impact of ICG use on anastomotic leakage rates and postoperative outcomes. METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic search of Medline, PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library was performed. The primary outcome was anastomotic leakage. Key secondary outcomes were conduit necrosis, mortality, and reoperation; all secondary outcomes were reported. The Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I) and Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tools were used for investigating risk of bias. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) was used to assess certainty of evidence. A random-effects meta-analysis and meta-regression as well as subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed. RESULTS: From 902 identified studies, 23 met the inclusion criteria (including 4 RCTs; 2845 patients, of whom 1154 underwent ICG assessment). ICG use was associated with reduced anastomotic leakage rates (OR 0.44 (95% c.i. 0.29 to 0.65), P < 0.001; number needed to treat = 13) and conduit necrosis rates (OR 0.32 (95% c.i. 0.12 to 0.85), P = 0.022). Mortality (OR 1.43 (95% c.i. 0.69 to 2.97), P = 0.335), reoperation (OR 0.84 (95% c.i. 0.51 to 1.39), P = 0.500), severe anastomotic leakage, overall morbidity, readmission, operating time, and length of stay did not differ between groups. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across all outcomes (GRADE), predominantly driven by the observational study design of many of the studies. CONCLUSION: Use of ICG appears to be associated with reduced anastomotic leak in oesophagectomy, although certainty of evidence is low. Assessment remains qualitative and operator-dependent.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Risk stratification before esophageal and gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) in older adults often relies on age and comorbidity; however, these measures may not capture vulnerability reflected in routinely collected claims data. We aimed to evaluate the claims-based frailty and short-term adverse events association after esophageal and gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection. METHODS: We used a nationwide Japanese administrative database to identify patients aged ≥ 75 years who underwent first esophageal or gastric ESD. Frailty was defined using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS), calculated from diagnoses during a 2 year lookback period. After 1:1 propensity score matching, frail and non-frail patients were compared. The primary outcome was binary composite of short-term adverse events, including in-hospital perforation/peritonitis, delayed bleeding, thromboembolism, aspiration pneumonia, and 30 day all-cause mortality. Component outcomes, survival, length of stay, costs, and readmission were also evaluated. RESULTS: Among 15,184 eligible patients, 4,970 matched pairs were included. CONCLUSION: Among older adults undergoing esophageal or gastric ESD, HFRS-defined claims-based frailty was associated with higher rates of short-term adverse events, particularly perforation/peritonitis and delayed bleeding. These findings suggest that routinely collected claims data may help identify vulnerable patients who warrant closer peri-procedural assessment and monitoring.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic interstitial lung disease with high morbidity and mortality. Inhaled treprostinil showed pulmonary vascular and lung-function signals in pulmonary hypertension associated with Interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and was subsequently tested in IPF trials. OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the efficacy and safety of inhaled treprostinil in adults with IPF. METHODS: PubMed, Google Scholar and the Cochrane Library/CENTRAL were searched for records published from January 2000 to 2026. A random-effects meta-analysis used the DerSimonian-Laird tau squared and inverse-variance weighting methods. Continuous outcomes were pooled as generic inverse-variance effects from reported estimates and 95% confidence intervals. Hazard ratios were pooled on the log scale. Safety outcomes were pooled as risk ratios from event counts. RESULTS: The searches identified 1552 records. After deduplication, 379 records were screened and 85 full-text reports were assessed. Eleven reports were included in the systematic review. TETON-1 and TETON-2 were the two direct-IPF randomized trials within the coordinated TETON program eligible for primary meta-analysis. Inhaled treprostinil improved absolute forced vital capacity (FVC) change at 52 weeks compared with placebo (MD 111.28 mL, 95% CI 77.61 to 144.95, p < 0.001; I squared 8.5%). Clinical worsening was reduced (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.57 to 0.84, p < 0.001; I squared 0.0%). Acute exacerbation was lower in pooled analysis (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.30 to 0.91, p = 0.022), while all-cause mortality did not differ significantly (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.47 to 1.05, p = 0.086). Adverse-event discontinuation, cough and headache were more frequent with treprostinil. CONCLUSIONS: In direct IPF randomized evidence, inhaled treprostinil preserved lung function and reduced clinical worsening at 52 weeks.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Global antibiotic use during the COVID-19 pandemic and its impact remain unclear. This study analysed antibiotic use, bacterial co-infections, and the association between antibiotic use and in-hospital mortality among patients hospitalised for COVID-19, using a WHO database. METHODS: We conducted a multicountry cohort study using anonymised patient-level data from The WHO Global Clinical Platform for COVID-19. Data were collected across 64 countries in all six WHO regions between January, 2020, and October, 2023. The study included hospitalised patients of all ages with suspected or confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. We obtained patient-level data from standardised WHO case report forms completed prospectively or retrospectively and from harmonised national registries, research studies, and hospital databases. Patients without a suspected or confirmed COVID-19 diagnosis or missing information on hospital admission date, antibiotic use, or outcome were excluded from the analysis. Patients were followed up from hospital admission until death, discharge, transfer, or 28 days, whichever occurred first. Follow-up data were collected at hospital discharge or death by the treating facility and entered into the platform. The primary outcome was 28-day in-hospital mortality, and we analysed this outcome using Cox proportional hazards models with a shared frailty term to account for country-level clustering. FINDINGS: The median age of the study population was 61·9 years (±21·7), with 198 223 women and 251 990 men with data available on antibiotic use. Of the 592 898 patients enrolled, 451 291 (76·1%) had data on antibiotic use and were included in the descriptive analysis; 122 854 had complete data on empirical treatment type, of whom 47 359 (38·5%) were included in the regression analysis. Among the 451 291 patients with data on antibiotic use, 341 125 (75·6%) received antibiotics, more frequently in severe to critical cases than in mild to moderate cases (80·5% vs 71·6%). Prescribing was highest in the Eastern Mediterranean (83·0%) and African (82·7%) regions and lowest in the Western Pacific region (32·8%), declining in the European region and region of the Americas but increasing in the African region between 2020 and 2022. Treatment was predominantly empirical and involved Watch antibiotics of the WHO Access, Watch, and Reserve classification. Clinically suspected co-infections were reported in 47 050 (7·9%) of the 592 898 patients; among those with positive cultures, 1815 (42·8%) of 4237 had multidrug-resistant bacteria. In the unadjusted analyses, empirical antibiotic use was associated with higher mortality across severity strata. After adjustment for age, sex, comorbidities, and disease severity, empirical antibiotic use remained associated with increased mortality in mild to moderate cases (adjusted hazard ratio 1·80, 95% CI 1·36-2·38) and severe to critical cases (1·16, 1·08-1·24). INTERPRETATION: Despite clinically suspected co-infections being reported in only 47 050 (7·9%) of the 592 898 enrolled patients, 341 125 (75·6%) of the 451 291 patients with data on antibiotic use received antibiotic therapy, predominantly broad-spectrum agents. As antibiotic use was not associated with improved clinical outcomes and is known to increase antimicrobial resistance, it should be rationalised through strengthened antimicrobial stewardship and behavioural interventions, particularly during respiratory viral epidemics. FUNDING: None.

papers.abstract_en: Patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain at high risk of relapse despite perioperative treatment1-3. NeoCOAST-2 (NCT05061550), a phase 2, randomised platform trial, tested novel perioperative treatments in patients with stage IIA-IIIB NSCLC. papers.abstract_en: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) lacks effective targeted therapies, and how metabolic reprogramming drives oncogenic signaling remains poorly defined. Here, we identify histone H3 lysine 23 lactylation (H3K23la) as a key epigenetic mediator linking lactate accumulation to tumor progression. H3K23la is upregulated in ESCC and correlates with poor prognosis. Mechanistically, H3K23la promotes WNK lysine deficient protein kinase 1 (WNK1) transcription, which increases histone H3 Ser10 phosphorylation (p-H3S10) and enhances AKT transcription, thereby driving PI3K-AKT signaling. This defines a lactate-H3K23la-WNK1-p-H3S10-AKT axis connecting metabolism to oncogenic signaling. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of WNK1 by CD03017 disrupts this pathway and suppresses tumor growth in vitro and in patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. In conclusion, our findings define a metabolic-epigenetic-signaling axis in ESCC and establish WNK1 as a potential therapeutic target downstream of histone lactylation.

papers.abstract_en: Previous studies have demonstrated promising results for radiolabeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET/CT in gastric cancer (GC) when compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT. In this prospective clinical trial, we assessed the impact of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) on primary staging and management of Danish patients with GC and gastroesophageal junction cancer (GEJC). Methods: Between February 8, 2024, and September 26, 2025, consecutive patients with GC or GEJC who were candidates for surgical resection and perioperative chemotherapy were included in this trial. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT images were deidentified and presented to the treating clinicians after the trial, at which point [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-based staging and tentative patient management were determined. Results: Twenty patients were included in the trial, including 15 (75%) with GEJC and 5 (25%) with GC; all patients were diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. For the primary tumor, [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 and [18F]FDG PET/CT agreed in 18 (90%) of cases, and both modalities demonstrated a detection rate of 90% (95% CI, 68%-99%). For clinical nodal staging, ceCT detected more lymph nodes than did [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and [18F]FDG PET alone (81 vs. 53 vs. 44, respectively). [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET did not detect additional lymph nodes beyond those detected with ceCT. Despite detecting fewer lymph nodes overall, [18F]FDG PET identified 6 additional lymph nodes in 5 patients, resulting in clinical nodal upstaging in 4 cases (20%) compared with both [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and ceCT. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET would have led to clinical metastatic upstaging in 4 patients (20%) because of the identification of potential distant metastases (1 peritoneal and 3 liver metastases), which would have resulted in a change in recommended patient management from curative-intent to palliative treatment in 3 patients (15%). Conclusion: The primary clinical value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET was its ability to detect distant metastases that were negative on [18F]FDG PET and ceCT, potentially impacting patient management. There were no obvious advantages in the evaluation of primary tumor and regional lymph nodes. Although the study population is relatively small and mostly consists of patients with GEJC, this study represents the first prospective investigation of consecutive patients in a well-defined, clinical northern European setting and indicates potential future roles for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET in GC and GEJC.

papers.abstract_en: Birt-Hogg-Dubé (BHD) syndrome is an autosomal dominant tumour predisposition disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the folliculin (FLCN) gene. It is characterized by benign skin tumours, renal neoplasia and cystic lung disease, with a risk of spontaneous pneumothorax. Although historically considered rare, population genomic data indicate that FLCN pathogenic variants are substantially more common than expected from clinically ascertained cases, suggesting that many variant carriers are not currently recognized in clinical practice. Advances in the molecular biology of BHD syndrome have established that FLCN loss-of-function is associated with dysregulation of the mTORC1-TFEB lysosomal signalling pathway, which has been implicated in mouse models of BHD syndrome-associated renal and lung pathology. Clinically, diagnosis relies on recognizing characteristic patterns across dermatological, renal and pulmonary presentations, with genetic confirmation enabling cascade testing and targeted surveillance. Management is centred on lifelong renal imaging, early intervention for tumours, and prevention and treatment of pneumothorax, delivered through multidisciplinary care. Despite generally indolent renal tumour behaviour, malignant progression can occur. Ongoing research aims to improve early diagnosis through population genomics and to develop targeted therapies. These advances are likely to transform the identification and management of BHD syndrome and provide broader insights into tumour suppressor biology.

papers.abstract_en: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem or stromal cells (MSCs) have shown therapeutic potential for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), yet reproducible and scalable methods to enhance EV yield and therapeutic potency remain limited. Here, we describe a biophysical priming strategy using pulsed focused ultrasound (pFUS) to apply controlled mechanical stimulation to umbilical cord (UC)-derived MSCs. A single, 1-min exposure generated primed EVs (pUC-EVs) with a 1.9-fold increase in concentration and a therapeutically enhanced molecular cargo, without changes in vesicle size distribution. We demonstrate that this process is mechanistically dependent on calcium influx, as calcium chelation with EGTA markedly reduced pFUS‑induced enhancement of EV secretion. Transcriptomic profiling of UC-MSCs indicated that pFUS activates calcium-dependent mechanotransduction pathways associated with endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRT) machinery, leading to coordinated upregulation of ESCRT components, vesicle trafficking regulators, while proteomics analysis of UC-EVs revealed enrichment of mitochondrial proteins that support oxidative phosphorylation and ATP generation. Functionally, pUC-EVs exhibit enhanced uptake by macrophages and alveolar epithelial cells, where they increase ATP levels, improve mitochondrial respiration, and promote a reparative, anti-inflammatory macrophage phenotype in vitro. In a lipopolysaccharide-induced juvenile ARDS model, intratracheal delivery of pUC-EVs localized treatment to the injured lung and significantly improved epithelial-endothelial barrier integrity, as shown by reduced vascular leakage, bronchoalveolar lavage protein content, inflammatory mediators, and neutrophil infiltration, alongside improved histological preservation compared with unprimed UC-EVs. A comprehensive in vivo safety assessment demonstrated that pUC-EVs exhibited significantly reduced serum IgG binding compared to UC-EVs, maintained normal coagulation parameter, and preserved organ function (liver, kidney, spleen) with no adverse histopathological changes, supporting a favorable biocompatibility profile. Together, these findings identify mechanopriming by pFUS as a mechanistically defined, well‑tolerated, and scalable approach to enhance EV biogenesis and therapeutic function, supporting the potential application of EVs as a therapy for ARDS and related inflammatory lung diseases.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The post-COVID-19 resurgence of pertussis has raised concerns regarding shifts in circulating Bordetella pertussis populations and increasing macrolide resistance. This study aims to characterize the population dynamics and clinically relevant genomic changes of B. pertussis in China and globally, and to develop a rapid visual assay for detecting the macrolide resistance-associated 23S rRNA A2047G mutation. METHODS: In this cross-sectional genomic epidemiology study, 22 recent clinical isolates were sequenced and analyzed with 7322 publicly available B. pertussis genomes. Global population structure was assessed using 7344 genomes, and Bayesian phylodynamic analysis was performed on 1054 temporally informative Chinese genomes selected from 1292 isolates collected during 1951-2024. We designed and optimized an allele-specific loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay incorporating a 3'-terminal artificial mismatch and a neutral red indicator for detection of the macrolide resistance-associated 23S rRNA A2047G mutation. Its analytical sensitivity and specificity were evaluated alongside quantitative PCR (qPCR) using serially diluted plasmids and 39 contrived DNA samples. papers.abstract_en: Lung transplantation (LTx) remains the only curative option for patients with end-stage pulmonary diseases. However, long-term outcomes are compromised by ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), a major contributor to primary graft dysfunction and chronic lung allograft impairment. Current pharmacological and technological strategies provide only partial protection, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic approaches. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic potential of extracellular vesicles derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC-EV) in a two-dimensional (2D) in vitro model of pulmonary IRI using A549 lung epithelial cells. To better recapitulate the in vivo airway microenvironment, we also employed a human airway organoid (hAO) model. Proteomic analysis of hiPSC-EV identified 1,698 proteins enriched in pathways relevant to apoptosis regulation, oxidative stress responses, and inflammatory signaling. In the 2D IRI model, the administration of hiPSC-EV during reperfusion significantly improved cell viability, reduced lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release, attenuated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and decreased apoptosis and necrosis. Furthermore, hiPSC-EV downregulated pro-inflammatory mediators (NFkB1, TNFα, IL1β, IL8, MCP1) while upregulating anti-inflammatory and anti-apoptotic key factors (IL1RA, BCL2). In the 3D model, hiPSC-EV administration preserved organoid structure and viability under IRI conditions, attenuated transcriptional and protein-level expression of pro-inflammatory and oxidative stress markers (IL1β, IL8, HMGB1, HMOX1), and enhanced anti-inflammatory (IL10) and cytoprotective (HSP27, HSP70) responses. Immunofluorescence further revealed that hiPSC-EV reduced activation of apoptotic and pyroptotic pathways. Moreover, intravenous administration of hiPSC-EV in mice showed no adverse safety signals, including tumorigenicity. Together, these findings demonstrate that hiPSC-EV exert broad cytoprotective effects in pulmonary IRI through coordinated regulation of inflammation, oxidative stress, and cell death. Their scalability, reproducibility, and favorable safety profile underscore their promise as innovative cell-free therapeutics to improve outcomes in LTx.

papers.abstract_en: Introduction: Bronchial thermoplasty (BT) reduces airway smooth muscle and may benefit severe asthma, but its role alongside biologics remains unclear. We assessed randomised and real-world evidence on efficacy and safety. Methods: We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane Library for RCTs and observational studies of BT in adults with severe uncontrolled asthma, analysing them separately. Conclusions: BT improved asthma-related quality of life and control, mainly in trials without sham controls, but increased short-term hospitalisation risk. Real-world findings were similar but came from uncontrolled studies. BT is not an established alternative to biologics, but may suit carefully selected patients with severe asthma who cannot use or do not respond to them.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary rehabilitation improves symptoms, exercise capacity and quality of life in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), although patients with similar clinical characteristics often show different responses. Cognitive impairment and obesity-related immune regulation further contributed to patient heterogeneity. papers.abstract_en: The clinicopathological significance and molecular basis of abnormal SMARCA2 expression in lung carcinoma remain poorly understood. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Oral corticosteroids (OCS) remain widely used in the treatment of severe asthma despite their adverse effects. Add-on biologic therapy offers the potential for minimizing OCS exposure. OBJECTIVE: This post hoc analysis of REALITI-A assessed the effect of mepolizumab on OCS use among subgroups of patients with severe asthma based on allergic/omalizumab-eligible phenotype and type-2 biomarker status. METHODS: REALITI-A was a prospective 2-year observational study among adults initiating mepolizumab for severe asthma. Endpoints assessed at 2 years were: change from baseline in daily maintenance OCS (mOCS) and total OCS dose, the proportion of patients discontinuing mOCS, the proportion of patients with 0 mg/day daily mOCS and total OCS dose, Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 scores, and clinically significant exacerbations. Outcomes were stratified by prior omalizumab use, omalizumab eligibility, baseline blood eosinophil count (threshold [<300/≥300 cells/μL] and category [<150/≥150-<300/≥300-<500/≥500 cells/μL]), baseline immunoglobulin E (IgE; <60/≥60-<190/≥190-<550/≥550 KU/L), atopic status (yes/no/unknown) and baseline fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO; <25/≥25-<50/≥50 parts per billion). RESULTS: Overall, 822 patients were included, with 39% receiving mOCS at baseline. For both mOCS and total OCS, median dose reductions after 2 years from baseline were 70-100% across all subgroups. Also, after 2 years, 44-71% of patients across subgroups had discontinued mOCS and 37-68% had 0 mg total OCS dose. CONCLUSION: These data highlight mepolizumab's effectiveness in reducing real-world OCS use across a broad range of patients with severe asthma, irrespective of omalizumab eligibility and baseline blood eosinophil count, IgE, atopic status, and FeNO.

papers.title_en: Local Delivery of Interferon-β1a for Respiratory Viral Infections: A Systematic Review.
papers.authors: Nayebhashemi M, Akhavan M, Foroohari A, Khayat S, Roshanzamir K, Shafaati M, Salehi M
papers.affiliation_highlight: CinnaGen Medical Biotechnology Research Center, Alborz University of Medical Sciences, Karaj, Iran.
papers.results: 24 项研究符合纳入标准，包括 12 项 RCT、7 项体外研究、1 项体内研究和 4 项专利报告；临床研究中显示抗病毒活性与免疫调节（如 ISG 上调、病毒载量下降）；临床获益在不同人群中不一致，在哮喘、COPD 和住院 COVID-19 患者中最为一致，其他试验的主要临床终点未显示显著改善；早期鼻病毒感染的预防性研究显示临床预防效力有限且不一致，尽管可检测到抗病毒活性；安全性总体耐受良好，不良事件以轻度、一过性为主
papers.authors_conclusion: 现有证据表明，鼻内或吸入 IFN-β 可增强抗病毒免疫，并在部分呼吸道病毒性疾病中（尤其抗病毒反应受损个体）提供临床获益；但对社区获得性上呼吸道感染的预防效力证据仍有限，需进一步研究确定最佳适应证、给药策略和目标人群
papers.ai_note: ①主要临床终点在多项试验中为阴性（摘要原文：other trials did not demonstrate significant improvements in their primary clinical outcomes），而摘要与结论以“抗病毒活性一致”“ISG 上调、病毒载量下降”等替代/机制学指标及哮喘、COPD、住院 COVID-19 的亚组人群作为获益支撑，存在以次要/替代终点替代主要终点的选择性强调倾向；②采用叙述性分层合成而非定量合并，全文未给出任何效应量、CI 或 P 值，无法判断获益幅度与精确度；③纳入专利与灰色文献（虽声明不作为疗效证据），仍可能影响“开发生态”叙述的完整性偏向；④人群、给药剂量与剂型高度异质，结论中“selected respiratory viral conditions”的界定依赖事后分层；⑤结论“provide clinical benefit”措辞强于所报告的主要终点结果，属乐观表述；⑥该主题与胸部肿瘤/胸外科无直接关联，对本领域临床判断的迁移价值有限

papers.abstract_en: Respiratory viral infections represent a major global health burden, with impaired antiviral interferon responses contributing to disease progression in several respiratory conditions. This systematic review evaluated the efficacy, safety, and biological effects of locally delivered intranasal or inhaled interferon-β1a (IFN-β1a), a host-directed antiviral therapy, across prophylactic, therapeutic, and experimental models of respiratory viral infections. A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, patent databases, and ClinicalTrials.gov up to July 2025. Peer-reviewed clinical and experimental studies, as well as relevant patent records, were identified. Patent and grey-literature sources were examined to provide a comprehensive overview of the development of locally delivered IFN-β1a and to identify relevant technological approaches that might not be captured in conventional bibliographic databases; however, these records were not considered evidence of clinical efficacy or safety. Eligible clinical and experimental evidence included randomized controlled trials (RCTs), in vitro, and in vivo studies. Owing to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesised using a structured narrative and stratified approach rather than quantitative pooling. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for RCTs, ToxRTool for in vitro studies, and the SYRCLE tool for in vivo studies. Twenty-four studies met the inclusion criteria, including 12 RCTs, seven in vitro studies, one in vivo study, and four patent reports. Preclinical evidence consistently demonstrated antiviral and immunomodulatory activity, including reduced viral replication and induction of interferon-stimulated genes. Clinical studies demonstrated consistent antiviral activity and immune modulation (e.g., ISG upregulation, viral load reduction). However, clinically meaningful benefit varied across populations and was most consistent in asthma, COPD, and hospitalised COVID-19 patients, whereas other trials did not demonstrate significant improvements in their primary clinical outcomes. Early prophylactic studies in rhinovirus infection showed limited and inconsistent clinical preventive efficacy despite detectable antiviral activity. Pharmacokinetic studies supported effective airway delivery, while safety findings indicated generally favourable tolerability with predominantly mild, transient adverse events. Available evidence indicates that intranasal or inhaled IFN-β may enhance antiviral immunity and provide clinical benefit in selected respiratory viral conditions, particularly among individuals with impaired antiviral responses. However, evidence for prophylactic efficacy against community-acquired upper respiratory tract infections remains limited, and further studies are required to define optimal indications, dosing strategies, and target populations.

papers.abstract_en: Single-inhaler triple therapy (SITT) combines an inhaled corticosteroid (ICS; for example, fluticasone furoate, budesonide, or beclometasone dipropionate), a long-acting β2-agonist (LABA; for example, vilanterol or formoterol fumarate), and a long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA; for example, umeclidinium or glycopyrronium bromide) in one device. Triple pharmacological therapy reduces exacerbations in selected patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), but its effects on mortality and cardiovascular outcomes remain uncertain. This structured narrative review summarizes randomized trials, observational comparative-effectiveness studies, target trial emulations, systematic reviews, and health technology assessments published between 2015 and 2026. We grouped the evidence by comparator: LABA/LAMA, ICS/LABA, multiple-inhaler triple therapy (MITT), and ICS continuation versus withdrawal, because each comparison addresses a different clinical question. Pivotal trials and evidence syntheses consistently showed fewer moderate-to-severe exacerbations with triple therapy, with reported rate ratios of approximately 0.69-0.93. Mortality signals from IMPACT and ETHOS are clinically important, but previous ICS use and ICS withdrawal among participants assigned to ICS-free comparators make these findings difficult to interpret. Observational cardiovascular findings are also uncertain because residual confounding, treatment selection, exposure misclassification, outcome misclassification, and differences in baseline disease severity limit causal interpretation. Compared with MITT, the main advantages of SITT are simpler treatment and possible improvements in adherence and persistence, not greater pharmacological potency. Treatment decisions should consider exacerbation history, repeated blood eosinophil counts, pneumonia risk, cardiovascular disease, previous ICS exposure and response, inhaler technique, device suitability, and patient preference. Trials in patients with documented absence of previous ICS use and well-designed target trial emulations are needed to determine whether the observed mortality and cardiovascular associations are causal.

papers.abstract_en: Patients with advanced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) respond differently to pulmonary rehabilitation (PR), and respiratory impairment alone might not fully explain this variability. Behavioral adaptation may contribute to differences in rehabilitation response. We studied 102 patients with advanced COPD (GOLD III-IV) who completed a 3-week multidisciplinary PR program. Functional response was assessed by change in six-minute walking distance (6MWD). Clinical, functional, psychological, lifestyle, and immune characteristics were evaluated, including coping strategies measured with the Brief COPE, Torque Teno virus (TTV) viremia, and circulating T-cell subsets. Exploratory mediation analyses examined whether coping strategies contributed to the association between age and rehabilitation response. Greater improvement in 6MWD was associated with higher active coping and planning scores, while self-distraction also differed across response groups. Planning scores were higher in good responders than in non-responders (7.10 ± 1.35 vs. 5.05 ± 1.93, respectively; p < 0.001). Planning was the only coping strategy showing a statistically significant indirect effect in the exploratory mediation analysis. The estimated proportion mediated was approximately 26.5%, although the wide confidence interval indicated substantial uncertainty. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational design and the assessment of multiple coping strategies. Conventional physiological measures, lifestyle characteristics, and immune biomarkers-including TTV viremia and circulating T-cell subsets-did not significantly distinguish rehabilitation response groups. Planning and active coping were associated with response in both sexes. A separate pilot randomized study, IMPROVE (n = 36), was subsequently conducted to investigate whether structured psychological support could influence coping strategies and help maintain the benefits of PR. At six months, patients receiving psychological support showed better maintenance of rehabilitation benefits, alongside improvements in psychological well-being, quality of life, and selected coping strategies. These findings provide preliminary evidence that coping-related characteristics may be modifiable; however, IMPROVE was a separate exploratory intervention study and was not designed to validate the observational findings. Assessment of coping strategies may complement clinical and functional evaluation and help identify patients who could benefit from tailored psychological support. Their clinical utility and the effectiveness of targeted interventions require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

papers.abstract_en: Chronic lung graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remains difficult to treat, and broad immunosuppression increases infection risk. Single-cell profiling of bronchoalveolar lavage from bronchiolitis obliterans lesions revealed collapse of an epithelial nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) metabolic axis with pathogenic immune-epithelial remodeling, nominating NAD+ restoration as an entry point. Because free NAD+ is poorly cell-permeable and rapidly consumed, we engineered CaNAD+-PGB-LiP (CNAPL), a high-payload NAD+ nanomedicine enabling direct intracellular replenishment. In murine allo-HSCT GVHD, CNAPL improved clinical scores and survival, reduced vascular and epithelial injury, and curtailed hyperinflammation and effector overactivation across GVHD target organs. Unlike immunosuppression, CNAPL preserved phagocytosis, NK/NKT cell (natural killer/natural killer T cell) cytotoxicity, and T cell memory. In posttransplant influenza or Klebsiella infection, CNAPL maintained pathogen control without rekindling GVHD, decoupling inflammation control from infection susceptibility. This metabolism-centered, host-directed strategy restores immune-tissue homeostasis and provides a practical translational path for durable lung GVHD control with preserved antimicrobial defense.

papers.abstract_en: Background Self-swab enhanced surveillance of respiratory pathogens is an emerging public health tool that could expand the reach of existing surveillance, providing real-time monitoring of circulating pathogens in the community. Methods We conducted a literature search using terms covering self-swabbing, respiratory infection, and surveillance. For inclusion, publications had to describe a study on the use of serial unsupervised self-swabbing for the purpose of tracking the frequency of respiratory infections in the general population. Results We found 42 publications originating from 27 unique studies on self-swab enhanced surveillance for respiratory infection. Twenty-six studies (96%) were conducted in a high-income setting. Eleven studies (41%) included children under the age of 12 years. Most studies involved a central laboratory conducting polymerase chain reaction testing on returned self-swabs which permitted testing for a wide range of pathogens. Among studies reporting the number of invitees, <20% of invited individuals typically agreed to join. In studies requiring regular symptom reporting, adherence was commonly >75%. Adherence rates for self-swab return were more variable (between 42-96%). Eight studies (30%) explored rapid antigen testing which appears to reduce the time taken between symptom onset and test result notification but limits the number of pathogens that can be evaluated compared with polymerase chain reaction testing. Based on our findings we present a list of suggestions to guide future implementation and investigation. Conclusions Further work is needed to characterise self-swab enhanced surveillance approaches that optimise community participation and protocol adherence, generate as close to real-time data as possible, and minimise costs.

papers.abstract_en: Pleural and thoracic air-leak complications after hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) are clinically important but underrepresented in broad post-transplant pulmonary reviews. Direct evidence is concentrated in adult allogeneic HCT. In a cohort of 618 adults, clinically significant pleural effusion had a 1-year cumulative incidence of 9.9% (95% confidence interval, 7.7-12.5%). A separate computed tomography-based cohort of 178 first allogeneic HCT recipients reported a day-100 cumulative incidence of 41.0%; these estimates are not directly comparable because the populations, ascertainment methods, endpoints, and follow-up differed. In 50 HCT recipients undergoing thoracentesis, a specific diagnosis was established in 26%, with 5 pneumothoraces and 0 hemothoraces. Thoracic air-leak syndrome is uncommon but carries poor outcomes in reported adult and pediatric series. This focused narrative review distinguishes direct HCT evidence from data extrapolated from hematologic malignancy, general pleural practice, critical care, interventional radiology, and cellular therapy. We organize evaluation by urgency, transplant phase, and radiographic pattern; define chronic graft-versus-host disease serositis as a diagnosis of exclusion; summarize chylothorax and pleural infection management; and provide procedure-specific safety considerations for thoracentesis, small-bore drainage, indwelling pleural catheters, intrapleural enzyme therapy, and pleural biopsy. No prospective HCT-specific trials validate these procedural pathways. Clinicians should therefore use ultrasound or image guidance; apply procedure-specific rather than uniform hemostatic thresholds; and integrate infection risk, platelet trajectory, anticoagulant exposure, oxygenation, operator setting, and expected benefit. The two clinical frameworks presented are proposed and non-validated.

papers.abstract_en: As humans spend most of their time indoors, they are continuously exposed to an array of indoor air pollutants. While exposure to individual indoor air pollutants may often occur at low levels, cumulative exposure to indoor air pollutants contributes substantially to the human exposome. Chronic inhalation of indoor air pollutants has been associated with multiple respiratory diseases, including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and respiratory infections. In this study, the cellular effects of an acute indoor dust exposure using a three-dimensional airway epithelial model were investigated. Bronchial epithelial cells (16HBE14o-) were cultured as spheroids and exposed to reference indoor dust (SRM 2585; 0-200 µg/mL) for 24 h. Metabolic activity, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, inflammatory cytokine secretion, and secretome profiles were assessed. Indoor dust exposure did not induce morphological alterations or significant reductions in metabolic activity. Instead, a concentration-dependent increase in intracellular ROS was observed. Cytokine analysis revealed selective cytokine modulation, while untargeted proteomics identified limited changes in individual protein abundance. Instead, pathway-level analyses revealed enrichment of epithelial differentiation-related pathways. Overall, these findings suggest that a 24 h indoor dust exposure may elicit subtle cellular responses rather than overt cytotoxicity or inflammatory activation. This study highlights the applicability of integrating functional, immunological, and proteomics-based approaches with 3D airway models to investigate cellular responses to complex environmental particle mixtures. However, direct extrapolation to human exposure scenarios is limited by uncertainties regarding effective cellular dose, particle localization and environmental representativeness. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory, hypothesis-generating observations.

papers.abstract_en: The SARS-CoV-2 Omicron subvariant JN.4 harbors a unique A475V substitution within the receptor binding domain (RBD) but exhibits limited expansion compared to its parallel descendant JN.1. Here, we investigate how hydrophobic remodeling within RBD large loop (residues 475-490) modulates receptor engagement and spike function. Cryo-electron microscopy reveals that A475V induces local remodeling of the receptor-binding motif (RBM) and alters the RBD-ACE2 interaction geometry. Local refinement revealed that the bulky valine substitution disrupts the local interaction network surrounding residue 475, resulting in a 3.5-fold reduction in ACE2-binding affinity compared with BA.2.86. In contrast to the L455S substitution in JN.1, which primarily alters the receptor-binding interface, A475V within the flexible large loop influences both local loop conformation and global spike conformational properties. Systematic mutagenesis identifies A475 and F486 as functionally constrained hydrophobic residues that preserve the structural framework of ACE2 engagement despite extensive sequence variation within the surrounding loop. Together with molecular dynamics simulations and functional assays, our findings establish the RBD 475-490 large loop as a structurally plastic yet functionally constrained element that balances receptor recognition, conformational stability, and antigenic diversification. These results provide a mechanistic framework for understanding region-specific evolutionary constraints that shape SARS-CoV-2 RBD adaptation.

papers.abstract_en: Auranofin, an FDA-approved oral anti-rheumatic drug, was previously shown by our group to restrict Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) replication and pathology in preclinical models. Here, we systematically characterized its mechanism of action (MOA) through biochemical drug-protein interactions, cell-based mechanistic assays, and preclinical efficacy studies. Auranofin directly binds and inhibits SARS-CoV-2 MPro while simultaneously targeting multiple stages of the viral life cycle, disrupting endosomal trafficking, suppressing Spike S1/S2 proteolytic processing, impairing syncytia formation, and attenuating NF-κB-driven proinflammatory signaling. In cell culture, Auranofin demonstrated robust synergy with Remdesivir but competed with the MPro inhibitor Nirmatrelvir, informing rational combination design. In mice infected with the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant, the oral combination of Auranofin and the Remdesivir prodrug GS-621763 outperformed monotherapy, markedly reducing viral replication, inflammatory cytokine responses, and lung pathology, and improving clinical outcomes. These findings establish a multi-target antiviral MOA of Auranofin and provide a mechanistic rationale for an all-oral antiviral combination regimen against COVID-19.

papers.abstract_en: AbstractHuman adenoviruses (HAdVs) are common respiratory pathogens that cause severe, life-threatening infections in immunocompromised individuals and children. Despite their medical importance, no clinically approved antiviral drugs exist. Here, we showed that 4H30, a 4-branched human defensin peptide, exhibited broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple HAdV subtypes in A549 and Calu-3 cells with negligible cytotoxicity and a high barrier to viral resistance in A549 cells. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that 4H30 exhibited a unique dual mechanism of action: direct virucidal activity through capsid disruption and endosomal trapping by impairing protein VI-mediated membrane penetration. Notably, 4H30 remained effective against HAdV-3 in human respiratory organoids and against HAdV-2 and HAdV-5 in an immunosuppressed hamster model, significantly reducing viral replication and disease-associated pathology. These findings demonstrate that 4H30 can inhibit multiple HAdVs through a novel mechanism, offering a new therapeutic avenue against HAdV infections.

papers.abstract_en: Legionella pneumophila is the causative agent of Legionnaires' disease, an accidental and severe form of pneumonia. The replication of L. pneumophila within alveolar macrophages requires the Dot/Icm type IV secretion system that translocates more than 330 bacterial effector proteins into the infected host cell. Many Dot/Icm effectors possess eukaryotic-like domains and manipulate host processes by functional mimicry. However, only a minority of effectors have been fully characterized. Redundancy among effector protein activities and host targets has complicated functional characterization of individual effector proteins. To explore the collective impact of Dot/Icm effectors on host cell processes, we created a library of 14 L. pneumophila genomic mutant strains lacking effector-rich regions (a total of 85 effector genes deleted) and used the multi-deletion mutants to interrogate host-pathogen interactions. While none of the mutants exhibited a defect in intracellular replication in THP-1 macrophages, several were attenuated in amoebae, including a mutant lacking a predicted amino acid transporter. In THP-1 cells, we observed that wild-type L. pneumophila 130b triggered a strong inflammatory and cellular stress transcriptional response in macrophages, whereas six mutants displayed reduced interferon signalling and one mutant displayed a marked decrease in the global expression of host heat shock response (HSR) genes. Through the creation of further sub-deletions, we found that the Dot/Icm effector kinase LegK4 was responsible for induction of the host HSR via the canonical transcription factor heat shock factor 1 (HSF1). Infection of THP-1 macrophages deficient in HSF1 revealed a potential role for the host HSR in the early stages of L. pneumophila infection. Together, these results reinforce the utility of multi-gene deletions to identify Dot/Icm effector phenotypes and the importance of the host HSR to L. pneumophila infection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: After a year of quiescence, SARS-CoV-2 activity increased rapidly in Hong Kong since June 2026. We sought to characterize the genomic profile of SARS-CoV-2 driving this COVID-19 surge in Hong Kong and to examine the global dissemination of the identified circulating lineages. METHODS: We performed SARS-CoV-2 whole-genome sequencing on archived respiratory specimens collected at Queen Mary Hospital, Hong Kong, between January 2025 and July 2026. Viral lineages were assigned via Nextclade. Global SARS-CoV-2 metadata downloaded from GISAID as of July 2026 were analyzed to track global evolutionary trends. RESULTS: Among 615 successfully sequenced strains, the XDV descendant NB.1.8.1 was the predominant lineage. Between April and July 2026, NB.1.8.1 descendants accounted for 95.6% (108/113) of sequenced strains, dominated by PQ.16.1.1 (81.5%). Spike substitutions 420N and 478 T emerged rapidly. While 478 T increased gradually throughout 2025, 420N emerged in April 2026 and reached 98.0% by June-July 2026. Strains harboring 420N-478 T dual substitution arose independently across distinct NB.1.8.1 lineages, accounting for 94.4% (102/108) of NB.1.8.1 descendants in Hong Kong during this period. Globally, the prevalence of NB.1.8.1 strains with 420N-478 T dual substitution increased from <1% before April 2026 to 50.7% by mid-July 2026, with the highest prevalence observed in Southeast Asia and Australia. CONCLUSIONS: The 2026 COVID-19 surge in Hong Kong was driven by NB.1.8.1 descendants harboring spike 420N and 478 T substitutions. The rapid worldwide expansion of these dual-substitution lineages highlights their competitive growth advantage and underscores the need for continued global genomic surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary fibrosis is a common and often fatal outcome of fibrosing interstitial lung diseases, characterized by progressive extracellular matrix deposition, destruction of alveolar architecture and irreversible loss of respiratory function. Although fibroblast activation and epithelial dysfunction are central to disease pathogenesis, fibrosis cannot be adequately explained by mesenchymal dysregulation alone. Rather, it represents a failure of multicellular repair regulation, in which immune cells, fibroblasts and epithelial populations reciprocally reshape cellular states, tissue niches and disease trajectories. Early innate immune responses amplify epithelial injury while simultaneously initiating provisional repair; however, when injury persists, these transient programmes fail to resolve and become stabilized into chronic profibrotic circuits involving monocyte-derived macrophages, dysfunctional T cells, inflammatory fibroblasts and matrix-producing myofibroblasts. Recent single-cell, spatial transcriptomic and lineage-tracing studies have revealed discrete cellular states, including SPP1⁺ scar-associated macrophages, inflammatory fibroblasts, CTHRC1⁺ myofibroblasts and tertiary-lymphoid-structure-associated stromal cells, that assemble multicellular, stage-specific and microanatomically restricted fibrotic niches. Collectively, these findings support a model in which soluble mediators, extracellular matrix mechanics, metabolic rewiring and immune-regulatory signalling cooperate to establish self-reinforcing stromal-immune circuits. In this Review, we synthesize current evidence for bidirectional immune-fibroblast crosstalk in pulmonary fibrosis, focusing on macrophage and T cell programmes, fibroblast-mediated immune regulation, spatiotemporal niche remodelling, mechanistic signalling networks, experimental models and therapeutic opportunities. We propose that progressive fibrosis reflects the spatiotemporal locking of pathological epithelial-immune-stromal circuits, a framework that may explain the limited efficacy of broad anti-inflammatory therapies in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and guide the development of more precise, stage-specific and combinatorial antifibrotic strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a threat to human health. Although receptor specificity, polymerase adaptation, and airway tropism have been studied extensively, it remains unresolved how they combine to shape tropism in airway epithelia. Here, we show that avian IAVs infect ciliated and secretory cells but preferentially bind to ciliated cells because of higher apical α2,3-linked sialic acid levels. As replication levels are comparable between cell types, this translates into overall preference for ciliated cells. Human IAVs also preferentially bind to ciliated cells despite comparable α2,6-linked sialic acid abundance. Instead, they show higher viral RNA and protein levels in secretory cells, linked to their compatibility with human ANP32 proteins and modestly higher ANP32A/B expression in this cell type, resulting in equal infection levels across cell types. Our findings redefine IAV tropism in the human airway as a stage-resolved process shaped by the interplay between apical glycans, viral binding, polymerase cofactor compatibility, and cell-type-specific replication capacity, moving beyond receptor-centric models.

papers.abstract_en: Robotic systems for computed tomography (CT)-guided needle insertion have been developed to address the limitations of conventional manual needle insertion. Thus far, various robotic systems have been clinically implemented, and accumulating evidence has suggested their clinical utility. The evidence has evolved beyond initial feasibility and early clinical experience to include larger observational and comparative studies. These studies have demonstrated high success rates of robot-assisted needle insertion in various CT-guided interventions, including thermal ablation, biopsy, and preoperative localization. Furthermore, an increasing number of comparative studies have demonstrated the advantages of robot-assisted procedures over conventional manual procedures. These advantages include improved needle insertion accuracy and reduced radiation doses to patients and/or physicians. Although most currently available robotic systems are needle-guiding robots designed to align a needle guide with a predetermined insertion trajectory, we have developed a CT-guided needle insertion robot capable of robotic needle advancement via remote control. Clinical studies have demonstrated the feasibility of robotic needle insertion using this system, as well as needle placement accuracy comparable to that of manual procedures, while eliminating radiation exposure to physicians. The integration of artificial intelligence and the implementation of telerobotic interventions are expected to contribute significantly to the further advancement of robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion. This narrative review summarizes the current clinical implementations and available evidence for robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion, including our system, and discusses future perspectives in this field.

papers.abstract_en: Developing effective nanomedicines for pulmonary metastasis remains challenging because of systemic clearance and local stromal barriers. Guided by single-cell transcriptomic profiling, we characterized a compartmentalized immunosuppressive network involving PGE2 and provide a biological rationale for coordinated EP2/EP4 antagonism. We therefore engineered an inhalable biomimetic platform (PD-1@E2/4 Exo) comprising PD-1-displaying exosomes co-loaded with EP2 and EP4 antagonists. Compared with intravenous administration, nebulized delivery increased pulmonary exposure of the engineered vesicles. Within the pulmonary tumor setting, surface PD-1 is intended to interfere with PD-1/PD-L1 signaling, while the co-delivered antagonists target the EP2/EP4 immunosuppressive axis. Treatment was associated with macrophage reprogramming, increased oxidative stress, and enhanced ICD-related responses in tumor cells. In the experimental breast-cancer lung-colonization model, the inhaled formulation reduced established pulmonary tumor burden and was accompanied by systemic immune-memory responses. These findings provide a preclinical study for integrating local pulmonary delivery with coordinated metabolic and immune modulation in breast cancer lung disease.

papers.abstract_en: AbstractInfluenza A virus (IAV) infection initiates a high-stakes competition for proteostatic control. While the host reconfigures its degradative machinery for defense, the virus simultaneously hijacks host proteostatic and degradative pathways to facilitate replication and evade immunity. Central to this conflict is the proteasomal switch, a process in which constitutive proteasome subunits (β1, β2, β5) are replaced by their inducible counterparts (β1i, β2i, β5i) to form the immunoproteasome (iP). Although iP is classically recognized for optimizing MHC class I antigen presentation, emerging evidence reveals more nuanced roles in IAV infections. This review synthesizes current knowledge on iP as an effector of host defense and target for viral subversion. We synthesize emerging evidence and propose working models detailing how IAV proteins may selectively interfere with proteasomal subunits to stabilize pro-viral factors. Furthermore, we examine the hypothesis that the iP functions alongside broader ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD), and autophagic pathways as a proteostatic buffer to mitigate proteotoxic and oxidative stress in the infected epithelium. By evaluating how age-related proteostatic decay and viral subversion could impair cellular clearance machinery, we provide a conceptual framework for understanding how proteasomal dysregulation contributes to acute lung injury and the chronic inflammatory state termed as inflammaging. Finally, we propose a hypothesis-generating, biphasic framework for timing-dependent proteasomal modulation, contrasting preclinically supported late-stage β5i inhibition against the theoretical concept of early-stage activation to highlight translational hurdles in severe influenza.
